analysis.title: 从模型竞速走向产品、算力与生态：本期 AI 趋势观察
analysis.lead: 本期共整理 129 条有效信号。下面不是新闻复述，而是把论文、公司、创业与政策放在同一张图里后的编辑性判断。
paragraphs: 研究侧共收录 20 条信号，重点包括 《BACE: LLM-based Code Generation through Bayesian Anchored…》、《Reward Hacking Benchmark: Measuring Exploits in LLM Agents…》。与只看榜单相比，更值得持续观察的是论文能否把 Agent 的可靠性、评测完整性与推理成本一起向前推进。
AI 跨领域贡献收录 16 条，代表性事件包括 《Claude Fable 5 协助找到雅可比猜想的显式三维反例》、《Building on our commitment to American scientific…》。这类结果会区分官方论文、可核验反例、媒体报道与尚待同行评审的社交平台首发，避免把‘可计算验证’和‘完成学术确认’混为一谈。
中国 AI 板块本期收录 16 条动态，已覆盖 Qwen / 通义千问、DeepSeek、字节豆包 / Seed。代表性变化包括 《英伟达重金力捧 “美版 DeepSeek ”将 发布 开源模型》、《通义千问 · Qwen -Image-2.1-Pro 透明图层+换背景全包了,小白也能用的＂轻量…》；竞争正在从单次模型发布延伸到开源策略、Agent 产品入口、国产算力适配和价格体系。
产业侧共有 30 条前沿实验室与大厂动态、14 条关键人物公开信号，另有 11 条创业和 10 条政策安全更新。模型能力、算力供给、创始人判断、产品分发与合规成本正在变成同一个竞争问题。

items.title: Introducing Quine: An AI research system designed for the complexity of biology
items.summary: Biology doesn't operate in silos, and neither should the AI representation of it. Quine is an early-stage research effort to create a multimodal world model of biology. By connecting insights across biological scales and modalities, Quine helps scientists computationally search a space far larger than intuition allows and prioritize hypotheses before they reach the lab. Experimental results provide important feedback, helping researchers sharpen future research directions. The post Introducing Quine: An AI research system designed for the complexity of biology appeared first on Microsoft Research .

items.title: BACE: LLM-based Code Generation through Bayesian Anchored Co-Evolution
items.summary: BACE treats generated code and tests as co-evolving populations instead of accepting synthetic tests as ground truth. Bayesian belief updates model tests as noisy sensors, while public examples anchor the search and reduce self-validating drift. The authors report strong results on LiveCodeBench v6 across proprietary and open-weight models.

items.summary: This paper describes a method for constructing inverse logic elements applicable to optical quantum computing and the key operations involved in building the entire inverse logic circuit. items.title: All-optical volatile memory dynamics for high-speed neuromorphic systems
items.summary: As artificial neural networks scale, conventional electronic transistors face severe speed and energy limitations. Optical platforms offer massive parallelism and bandwidth, yet existing short-term memory elements often rely on inefficient optical-to-electrical-to-optical conversions. To overcome this barrier, we introduce a comprehensive mathematical foundation for feedback-free, intensity-encoded photonic memory devices. By leveraging delayed optical nonlinearity within resonant cavities, we successfully demonstrate history-dependent signal processing entirely in the optical domain.

items.title: Certified Program Synthesis with a Multi-modal Verifier
items.summary: Certified program synthesis (aka vericoding) is the process of automatically generating a program, its formal specification, and a machine-checkable proof of their alignment from a natural-language description. Two challenges make vericoding difficult. First, specifications synthesised from natural language are often either too weak to be meaningful or too strong to be implementable, yet existing approaches lack systematic means to detect such defects. items.summary: Formal verification provides the highest assurance of software correctness and security, but its application to large-scale, evolving systems remains a major challenge. items.title: QUTest: A Native Testing Framework for Quantum Programs
items.summary: Quantum programs are often shared as OpenQASM 3 circuits, but tests are still written in host languages such as Python with Qiskit. We present QUTest, a native framework in which both programs and tests are standard .qasm files. Tests follow the Arrange / Act / Assert pattern, while configuration, runtime requirements, and assertions are encoded as pragma comments (//%), preserving compatibility with existing OpenQASM tools. items.title: Safeguarding LLM Agents from Misalignment through Provenance Analysis
items.summary: As LLM agents gain increasing access to powerful tools, ensuring that their actions align with the user's intent becomes critical. When an agent's proposed action deviates from that intent---a phenomenon called misalignment---it may cause harm that is difficult to undo. Existing runtime guardrails rely on an LLM-as-a-judge paradigm that lacks a systematic framework for reasoning about alignment, often producing inconsistent or difficult-to-audit judgments. Motivated by provenance analysis, we propose a conceptual framework that formalizes misalignment detection as determining whether a proposed tool call is supported by traceable evidence in the agent's context.
